column1: # Step 5's cheats: the ways to show the milestone without doing the work.
# Two rules, and both are about the same move. This is the step at which the
# repository's own test suite becomes losable: on JDK 17 the forked JVM dies in
# `StorageUtils` before any test body runs -- 256 errors where the same tree at
# JDK 8 reports 0 -- and the step asks for that fork to be opened onto
# `java.base/sun.nio.ch` (m05.tsv, m2). The cheap way to make a red suite stop
# being red is not to open the module but to stop running the suite, and these
# two rules price that.
#   `skipTests` / `skip`  surefire reads both its own `<configuration>` and the
#                         properties of the same name, and test.sh does not
#                         pass `-DskipTests=false`, so either spelling in the
#                         candidate pom turns `mvn test` into a no-op that
#                         exits 0. `pom pluginconfig` is flattened from every
#                         `<configuration>` under the plugin and `pom prop` is
#                         the effective properties, so the two rules cover the
#                         two places the setting can live.
# What is deliberately *not* here, because it is inert rather than allowed:
#   growing `<excludes>`  the pom already excludes nine test classes, and
#                         test.sh runs the suite with `-Dtest=**/*Test.java`,
#                         which overrides surefire includes and excludes both.
#                         The evidence is this task's own: the excluded
#                         `CustomReportServiceTest` runs in every measured arm
#                         and its two failures are counted, which is why they
#                         are exempted by name rather than by the pom
#                         (step04/test.sh). A rule forbidding a longer exclude
#                         list would be a rule about nothing, and a gate full
#                         of rules about nothing is how a gate stops being
#                         read.
#   deleting src/test     test.sh removes /app/src/test and copies a pristine
#                         overlay over it before the suite runs, so the tests
#                         that execute are never the candidate's copy of them.
#   `testFailureIgnore`   test.sh already passes
#                         `-Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true` and reads the
#                         surefire XML rather than maven's exit code, so
#                         setting it changes nothing that is read.
#   `<forkCount>0</...>`  running the tests inside maven's own JVM makes
#                         `<argLine>` inert. What it does not do is fail
#                         `m2-test-jvm-opens`: that rule reads `pom
#                         testjvmarg`, which pom-scan.py derives from the
#                         argLine's arguments and nothing else, so a pom that
#                         carries the open and also sets `forkCount` to zero
#                         still emits the argument and still satisfies the
#                         rule. The rule cannot see the fork at all. What
#                         prices the move is the suite: maven's own JVM is not
#                         opened either, so `StorageUtils` throws while the
#                         session starts, every test body is an error before it
#                         runs, and the `tests` family pays out on the count it
#                         reads from the surefire XML. The candidate keeps the
#                         requirement and loses the behaviour, which is the
#                         right way round for a move that is a real -- if
#                         unusual -- build configuration rather than a dodge.
#                         No fork rule is added for it. The fact would have to
#                         come from the shared pom scanner, and steps 1-4 have
#                         been scored and signed off against the bytes that
#                         scanner has now; growing it to emit a fork count
#                         would invalidate their measurements in order to fence
#                         a move that already loses its own family. It is named
#                         in instruction.md as "the forked test JVM" so that
#                         the shape being asked for is stated rather than
#                         inferred.
# The read-site dodges -- hiding a format behind a variable, moving the options
# into a map, deleting the read -- are fenced inside the requirement that would
# otherwise reward them (m05.tsv, m3) rather than repeated here.
# The rule this file used to carry, `no-inferred-schema-fed-back`, went with
# the json clause it was about: with nothing in the gate asking for a declared
# schema, reading a schema back off a Dataset buys nothing, and a prohibition
# on a move that pays nothing is a rule about nothing (NOTES 6.5.2).
no-tests-skipped-config
column5: the candidate pom configures surefire to skip the tests; the suite this step makes passable again is graded by running it, and a suite that does not run is not a suite that passes

column1: no-tests-skipped-property
column5: the candidate pom sets a property that skips the tests, which is the same move as configuring it on the plugin with the setting spelled somewhere surefire also reads
